patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, vomiting. Reports bloody loose bowel movements.

questions: Where exactly is the abdominal pain located (e.g., right upper quadrant, left upper quadrant, periumbilical, lower abdomen), and does it radiate to the back or groin?
Do you have any vomiting of blood or black/tarry stools?
Did the pain start suddenly and become rapidly severe, and do you have a “board-like” hard abdomen when you touch or press it?
Have you been taking NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen/naproxen) or aspirin recently, or do you have a history of peptic ulcer disease?
Have you had any fever, worsening pain with breathing, or pain when the doctor presses and releases your abdomen (rebound tenderness)?
Have you had any black, tarry stools or vomited coffee-ground material today, even once?
Have you had any recent black/coffee-ground *vomiting* or severe sudden “worst” abdominal pain that began abruptly?
Have you had any measured fever and/or chills, and do you have worsening pain when moving, coughing, or with abdominal jarring (to suggest peritonitis)?
Have you had any dizziness, fainting, or symptoms of low blood pressure (e.g., feeling very weak when standing) since the pain started?
Have you had any recent unintentional weight loss or trouble swallowing (dysphagia)?
answers: “It's located in the upper middle part of my abdomen, kind of the epigastric area, and it doesn’t really radiate to my back or groin.”
“No, I haven’t vomited any blood, and I haven’t noticed black or tarry stools.”
“No, it didn’t start suddenly; it came on over the past couple of hours and hasn’t become rapidly severe. My abdomen isn’t hard or board-like when you press on it.”
“Mostly I take over-the-counter painkillers for my knee, which I think are NSAIDs like ibuprofen. I don’t have a known history of peptic ulcer disease, and I haven’t taken aspirin specifically.”
“No fever that I’ve noticed, and the pain doesn’t get worse when I breathe in. When you press and then release my abdomen, it feels tender but I don’t feel sharp worsening or a rebound-type pain.”
“No, I haven’t had any black or tarry stools, and I haven’t vomited anything that looks like coffee grounds today.”
“No, I haven’t had any black or coffee-ground vomiting, and it hasn’t been the ‘worst’ sudden pain—it's been coming on gradually over the past couple of hours.”
“I haven’t measured any fever or had chills, and the pain doesn’t noticeably worsen when I move, cough, or jolt.” “It mainly feels like cramping/pressure in the epigastric area.”
“I haven’t felt dizzy or faint, and I haven’t noticed any weakness when standing or symptoms of low blood pressure since the pain started.”
“Yes, I’ve had unintentional weight loss over the past couple of months because I’ve been avoiding eating due to the pain. I haven’t noticed any trouble swallowing.”
